\section{Columns before figure}
Introductory text in the first column precedes a figure that spans both
columns. Enough synthetic prose fills the left column so a MULTI\_COLUMN
band exists above the spanning figure instead of a single leftover stack.

Column recovery should keep these sentences in the left column until the
column is full. The next paragraph continues the same contract: reading
order visits left-column text before right-column text, and the later
figure is a spanning band rather than a third column.

Further filler repeats layout-invariant language so the compiled PDF stays
deterministic. Band detection may split display gaps, but at least one
body strip on this page must contain two columns once the left column
fills.

A second left-column paragraph continues until the column is visually
full. Only then does the next section heading belong in the right column
in the compiled article.

Still more left-column prose records that a spanning figure is not a
column. The recovery engine must wait until this stack reaches the bottom
of the first column before wrapping. Extra sentences about gutters,
bands, and captions exist only to occupy space.

A closing left-column note restates the reading-order contract one last
time. Left column first, then right column, then the spanning figure on
the following page. This paragraph should be among the last blocks that
still sit in the left column.
